findings.evidence: The prose calls k[t^2,t^3] -> k[t] bijective. Its image omits t, as ex-normalization-cusp proves in step 6.1. The normalization morphism is bijective on classical points; its coordinate-ring pullback is not surjective. A bijective ring homomorphism would be an isomorphism.

The summary states that the node fibre consists of two points t=±1 and is not unibranch, without the characteristic-not-two restriction explicitly required by ex-normalization-node. In characteristic two, 1=-1 and t^2-1=(t-1)^2, so this fibre has one classical point and the asserted two-point conclusion fails.

The conductor generators t^2,t^3 are called the first two semigroup elements. The numerical semigroup <2,3> begins 0,2,3; its first two elements would give t^0=1 and t^2, generating the whole ring rather than the conductor. They are the first two positive elements, as the repaired ex-conductor-cusp-semigroup now states.
